chunks: Have they appointed intercessors other than God? Say: "Even though they have no power in the least, nor do they understand?"
ai.seo_question: Who are the intercessors besides God mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Surah Az-Zumar, this verse critiques the polytheists' reliance on intermediaries by highlighting their inherent lack of power (malak) and intellect ('aql), a key criterion in Shia theology for valid intercession. It underscores that true shafa'ah belongs solely to Allah, who grants it only to those He approves, thereby refuting the notion of autonomous divine agents. This aligns with the Shia understanding that intercession is not an independent right of the saints but a permission-based grace from God.
